title: GMAT: Quant Formulas and Rules

sources.name: Original educational synthesis from general knowledge

description: For GMAT learners reviewing arithmetic, algebra, number properties and word-problem rules. Original prompts emphasize assumptions, useful formulas and common calculation traps.

cards.front: What is percent change from a positive original value A to a new value B?
cards.back: 100(B - A)/A percent. Use the original value as the denominator.

cards.front: How do you calculate p percent of x?
How do you increase x by p percent?
cards.back: Multiply x by 1 + p/100.

cards.front: How do you decrease x by p percent?
cards.back: Multiply x by 1 - p/100.

cards.front: How do successive percentage changes combine?
cards.back: Multiply their growth factors; do not add the percentages.

cards.front: What is the net effect of a 20% rise followed by a 20% fall?
cards.hint: The second percentage uses a different base.

cards.front: A price after a 25% increase is 150. What was it originally?
How do percentage points differ from percent change?
cards.back: Percentage points are the subtraction of two percentages. Relative percent change divides that difference by the original percentage.

cards.front: How do you split a total T in the ratio a:b?
cards.back: The shares are aT/(a+b) and bT/(a+b), for positive a and b.

cards.front: How can ratios a:b and b:c be combined?
cards.back: Rescale so the shared b component matches, then read a:b:c.

cards.front: What is the arithmetic mean of n values?
cards.back: Their sum divided by n.

cards.front: How do you recover a sum from a mean and a count?
cards.back: Sum = mean × count.

cards.front: What is a weighted mean?
cards.back: Sum of each value times its weight, divided by the sum of the weights.

cards.front: How do you combine the means of groups with sizes n and m?
cards.back: Combined mean = (n × first mean + m × second mean)/(n+m).

cards.front: How is the median found for an odd number of observations?
cards.back: Sort the observations; take the middle value.

cards.front: How is the median found for an even number of observations?
cards.back: Sort the observations; average the two middle values.

cards.front: What is the mode of a data set?
cards.back: A value occurring most often. There may be multiple modes or no uniquely most frequent value.

cards.front: What is the range of a data set?
cards.back: Maximum minus minimum.

cards.front: What happens to the mean when c is added to every value?
cards.back: It increases by c.

cards.front: What happens to standard deviation when c is added to every value?
cards.back: It stays the same.

cards.front: What happens to standard deviation when all values are multiplied by k?
cards.back: It is multiplied by the absolute value of k.

cards.front: When is the standard deviation zero?
cards.back: When all observations are equal.

cards.front: What is distance in terms of constant rate and time?
cards.back: Distance = rate × time, using compatible units.

cards.front: What is average speed over an entire journey?
cards.back: Total distance divided by total elapsed time.
cards.hint: Combine distances and times before dividing.

cards.front: What is average speed for equal distances traveled at positive speeds a and b?
cards.back: 2ab/(a+b).

cards.front: What is average speed for equal times traveled at speeds a and b?
What is the closing speed of two objects moving toward each other?
cards.back: The sum of their speeds along the line joining them.

cards.front: What is the relative speed when one object overtakes another in the same direction?
cards.back: Faster speed minus slower speed.

cards.front: How do you express a worker's rate if a job takes t hours?
cards.back: 1/t jobs per hour, assuming a constant rate.

cards.front: How do independent constant work rates combine?
cards.back: Add rates when workers contribute to the same job; subtract a rate that undoes work.

cards.front: If workers take a and b hours alone, how long together?
cards.back: ab/(a+b) hours, assuming constant independent rates and one shared job.

cards.front: What is the basic mixture equation?
cards.back: Amount of desired component = concentration × total mixture amount, with concentration as a fraction.

cards.front: How do you compute concentration after mixing two compatible solutions?
cards.back: Total amount of solute divided by total solution amount, assuming amounts are additive.

cards.front: What is simple interest?
cards.back: I = Prt, where P is principal, r is annual decimal rate, and t is years.

cards.front: What is compound value with n equal compounding periods per year?
cards.back: A = P(1+r/n)^(nt), for annual nominal rate r and t years.

cards.front: What is profit in terms of revenue and cost?
cards.back: Profit = revenue - cost.

cards.front: How is markup on cost calculated?
cards.back: 100 × profit/cost percent, when cost is positive.

cards.front: How is profit margin on revenue calculated?
cards.back: 100 × profit/revenue percent, when revenue is positive.

cards.front: What is the break-even quantity with fixed cost F, unit price p, and variable unit cost v?
cards.back: F/(p-v), assuming p > v and a linear cost model; round up for whole units when necessary.

cards.front: How do you add fractions a/b and c/d?
cards.back: Use a common denominator: (ad+bc)/(bd), with b and d nonzero.

cards.front: How do you divide a/b by c/d?
cards.back: Multiply by the reciprocal: ad/(bc), with b, c and d nonzero.

cards.front: When can a factor be canceled from a fraction?
cards.back: When it is a common nonzero multiplicative factor of the entire numerator and denominator.

cards.front: For positive fractions, when is a/b greater than c/d?
cards.back: When ad > bc, provided b and d are positive.

cards.front: What makes a rational number's reduced decimal expansion terminate?
cards.back: Its denominator has no prime factors except 2 and 5.

cards.front: What is 0.125 as a fraction in lowest terms?
What is 0.375 as a fraction in lowest terms?
What is 0.625 as a fraction in lowest terms?
What is 0.875 as a fraction in lowest terms?
What is 0.333... as an exact fraction?
What is the remainder representation of an integer N divided by positive integer d?
cards.back: N = dq + r, where q is an integer and 0 ≤ r < d.

cards.front: What is a prime number?
cards.back: An integer greater than 1 whose only positive divisors are 1 and itself.

cards.front: Is 1 prime?
cards.back: No. It has only one positive divisor.

cards.front: What is the only even prime?
What is the greatest common divisor of two positive integers from their prime factorizations?
cards.back: The product of shared primes raised to the smaller exponent in the two factorizations.

cards.front: What is the least common multiple from prime factorizations?
cards.back: The product of every prime appearing, raised to its larger exponent.

cards.front: How are gcd and lcm related for positive integers a and b?
cards.back: gcd(a,b) × lcm(a,b) = ab.

cards.front: How many positive divisors does p^a q^b have for distinct primes p and q?
When is an integer divisible by 3?
cards.back: When its digit sum is divisible by 3.

cards.front: When is an integer divisible by 9?
cards.back: When its digit sum is divisible by 9.

cards.front: When is an integer divisible by 4?
cards.back: When its last two digits form a number divisible by 4.

cards.front: When is an integer divisible by 8?
cards.back: When its last three digits form a number divisible by 8.

cards.front: When is an integer divisible by 6?
cards.back: When it is divisible by both 2 and 3.

cards.front: When is an integer divisible by 5?
cards.back: When its last digit is 0 or 5.

cards.front: What is the parity of the sum of two odd integers?
cards.back: Even.

cards.front: What is the parity of the sum of an odd and an even integer?
cards.back: Odd.

cards.front: When is a product of integers odd?
cards.back: Exactly when every factor is odd.

cards.front: How can consecutive integers be represented algebraically?
cards.back: n, n+1, n+2, and so on, where n is an integer.

cards.front: How can consecutive even integers be represented?
cards.back: 2n, 2n+2, 2n+4, and so on.

cards.front: What is the sum of the first n positive integers?
What is the sum of the first n positive odd integers?
What is n factorial for positive integer n?
What is 0 factorial?
How do you count trailing zeros in n! in base ten?
cards.back: Count factors of 5: floor(n/5) + floor(n/25) + floor(n/125) + ... until terms are zero.

cards.front: What is the multiplication rule for counting choices?
cards.back: Multiply the number of choices at each stage when each prior choice permits the stated number of next choices.

cards.front: What is the number of ordered selections of r items from n distinct items without replacement?
What is the number of unordered selections of r items from n distinct items?
How many arrangements of n objects exist when groups of sizes a, b, ... are internally identical?
cards.back: n!/(a!b!... ), where group sizes sum to n.

cards.front: What is probability in a finite equally likely sample space?
cards.back: Favorable outcomes divided by total outcomes.

cards.front: What is the complement rule for probability?
cards.back: P(not A) = 1 - P(A).

cards.front: What is the addition rule for two events?
cards.back: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B).

cards.front: How do you multiply probabilities for independent events?
cards.back: P(A and B) = P(A)P(B).

cards.front: What is conditional probability P(A given B)?
cards.back: P(A and B)/P(B), provided P(B) > 0.

cards.front: How can you find the probability of at least one success?
cards.back: 1 minus the probability of zero successes.

cards.front: For n independent trials with success probability p, what is the probability of zero successes?
What is the two-set inclusion-exclusion formula for counts?
cards.back: Count(A union B) = count(A) + count(B) - count(A intersection B).

cards.front: What is a^m × a^n?
cards.back: a^(m+n), where the powers are defined.

cards.front: What is a^m/a^n for nonzero a?
What is (a^m)^n for integer exponents?
cards.back: a^(mn), where defined.

cards.front: What is a^0 for nonzero a?
What is a^(-n) for nonzero a?
What is the principal square root of x^2 for real x?
cards.back: The absolute value of x.
cards.hint: A principal square root is nonnegative.

cards.front: When is sqrt(ab) = sqrt(a)sqrt(b) valid for real square roots?
cards.back: When a and b are both nonnegative.

cards.front: What is the difference-of-squares identity?
What is the expansion of (a+b)^2?
What is the expansion of (a-b)^2?
How do you solve ax+b=c when a is nonzero?
cards.back: x = (c-b)/a.

cards.front: What happens when an inequality is multiplied or divided by a negative number?
cards.back: Reverse the inequality sign.

cards.front: What does the zero-product rule say?
cards.back: If ab = 0 for real numbers, then a = 0 or b = 0, or both.

cards.front: What is the quadratic formula for ax^2+bx+c=0 with a nonzero?
What does a quadratic discriminant greater than zero imply?
cards.back: Two distinct real roots.

cards.front: What does a quadratic discriminant equal to zero imply?
cards.back: One repeated real root.

cards.front: What does a quadratic discriminant less than zero imply?
cards.back: No real roots.

cards.front: For ax^2+bx+c=0, what is the sum of its roots?
cards.back: -b/a, counting roots with multiplicity and assuming a is nonzero.

cards.front: For ax^2+bx+c=0, what is the product of its roots?
cards.back: c/a, counting roots with multiplicity and assuming a is nonzero.

cards.front: What does absolute value represent on the number line?
cards.back: Distance from zero, so it is never negative.

cards.front: For c > 0, how do you solve absolute value of x less than c?
cards.back: -c < x < c.

cards.front: For c > 0, how do you solve absolute value of x greater than c?
cards.back: x < -c or x > c.

cards.front: What must be checked after squaring both sides of an equation?
cards.back: Check each candidate in the original equation, because squaring can introduce extraneous solutions.

cards.front: What values are excluded from a rational expression's domain?
cards.back: Values making any original denominator zero, even if a factor later cancels.

cards.front: What is the slope between distinct points (x1,y1) and (x2,y2)?
cards.back: (y2-y1)/(x2-x1), provided x2 differs from x1.

cards.front: What is slope-intercept form of a nonvertical line?
cards.back: y = mx+b, where m is slope and b is the y-intercept.

cards.front: What is the slope of a horizontal line?
What is the slope of a vertical line?
cards.back: Undefined.

cards.front: What is the nth term of an arithmetic sequence with first term a1 and common difference d?
What is the sum of n terms of an arithmetic sequence?
cards.back: n(first term + last term)/2.

cards.front: What is the nth term of a geometric sequence with first term a1 and ratio r?
How can you compare two positive quantities using their squares?
cards.back: Squaring preserves their order because squaring is increasing for nonnegative numbers.

cards.front: What does a negative number times a negative number equal in sign?
cards.back: Positive.

cards.front: How do you convert hours to minutes?
cards.back: Multiply by 60.

cards.front: How do you convert kilometers per hour to meters per second?
cards.back: Divide by 3.6.
